facts.claim: Primitive is email infrastructure built for AI agents.

Primitive provides one-call email sending/receiving, managed *.primitive.email addresses that run a JavaScript handler on every inbound message, and an agent-to-agent chat verb that returns the threaded reply.
Inbound messages can be delivered to a webhook endpoint or processed by a hosted JavaScript Function running on every received message.

Primitive requires bearer tokens (API keys prefixed prim_ or OAuth tokens prefixed prim_oat_) for endpoints that read/modify customer data, and tokens are scoped to a single organization; tenant isolation prevents one org from accessing another org’s mailbox contents/functions/memories.
Outbound mail is signed/authenticated with managed DKIM, SPF, DMARC, and TLS-RPT, and domain authentication records are generated and verified through the API.
Webhook deliveries are signed with HMAC-SHA256 so receivers can verify authenticity before acting.
Primitive provides an agent authorization mechanism using a DNS TXT record (_agents) that controls which agents/platforms may email a domain (accept/reject and allow lists).
Primitive does not auto-delete stored inbound mail on a schedule; inbound message contents are retained until deleted.
Primitive’s trust/security documentation states authentication, data isolation, and message integrity are core to the product and describes how its security boundaries work.

incidents_or_risks.what: Hosted Functions, Wake schedules, x402 payments, and custom domains are gated on the free agent plan and return a plan or entitlement error until the account is upgraded.
Signup through the third-party listing is rate-limited per IP, returning HTTP 429 after several new accounts per day.
The send-mail endpoint accepts exactly one recipient and has no CC, BCC, custom header, tags, or metadata fields, which limits fan-out and fallback use.

facts.claim: Primitive describes itself as Y Combinator-backed email infrastructure for AI agents, with a small team based in San Francisco.
The inbound MX implementation and the Node.js, Python, and Go SDKs are published publicly on GitHub.
Primitive's REST API is versioned under /v1, and breaking changes are released under a new version rather than altering an existing one.
Primitive says it manages inbound MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, TLS-RPT, bounce processing, and sending-IP reputation.
Inbound email content is retained until the user deletes it, and Primitive does not auto-delete stored mail on a schedule.
Webhook deliveries from Primitive are signed so receivers can verify authenticity before acting on a message.
Primitive publishes machine-readable descriptions such as an OpenAPI specification, an llms.txt file, and an MCP discovery document so agents can find and use it.
Primitive's MCP server is listed in public registries and works with Claude, Cursor, VS Code agent mode, and Goose.
Primitive lists a free plan that covers sending, replying, inbound listing and search, threads, filters, webhook endpoints, and durable Memories.
Primitive's send-mail API requires a verified outbound domain for the sending organization, and the sender API key uses a prim_ prefix.
Primitive's send endpoint supports idempotency keys so a retried send with the same key and body replays the original result rather than sending twice.
